cards.text: This is the vision Isaiah the prophet saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1), and this part starts in wartime. Ahaz son of Jotham is king of Judah, and Rezin, king of Aram, marches up to wage war against Jerusalem. With him comes Pekah son of Remaliah, the king of Israel.

cards.question: Rezin and Pekah march on Jerusalem together. True or false: they manage to overpower the city.

cards.text: Then word reaches the house of David that Aram is in league with Ephraim, which is Pekah's kingdom of Israel. Two kings, one team, and they're both looking at Judah.

cards.question: When Ahaz and his people hear that Aram is in league with Ephraim, what do their hearts do?

answers.text: Tremble like trees in the wind
Stand tall like cedars on a hill
Burn like fire in dry brush

cards.text: Shaking like a tree in the wind? Friend, I did that for YEARS every time the junk drawer rattled open. Then the LORD sends Isaiah the prophet out to meet Ahaz, and Isaiah's not going alone.

cards.question: Isaiah goes out to meet Ahaz, and he brings his ___ Shear-jashub with him.

cards.text: They meet at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field. And Isaiah has a message from the LORD for Ahaz.

cards.question: Two kings are coming and Ahaz is shaking. True or false: the LORD's message tells Ahaz to gather his army and march out to fight.

cards.text: The LORD's message starts, "Calm down and be quiet." Then He tells Ahaz not to be afraid or disheartened over these two kings, and He gives them a nickname.

cards.question: What does the LORD call Rezin and the son of Remaliah, the two kings Ahaz is so afraid of?

answers.text: Two roaring lions in the hills

cards.text: Ahaz is trembling over the stuff I sweep out of my oven at closing time! But those two stubs have plotted his ruin: invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among themselves.

cards.question: Once Judah is divided up, who do Aram and Ephraim plan to set up as king over it?

cards.text: They're picking a king for a throne that isn't theirs, like measuring for curtains in a house they don't own. Then the Lord GOD speaks.

cards.question: True or false: the Lord GOD says the plan of Aram and Ephraim against Judah will happen.

cards.text: The Lord GOD says, "It will not arise; it will not happen." Then He names who's in charge: the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin.

cards.question: God says that within sixty-five years, Ephraim will be ___ as a people.

cards.text: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. That's the WHOLE chain of command, friend, two men at the top.

cards.question: God ends with a warning for Ahaz: if he doesn't stand firm in something, he won't stand at all. What is it?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Ahaz again. This time He offers Ahaz something he can SEE.

cards.question: The LORD tells Ahaz to ask the LORD his God for a ___.

cards.text: And it can be anything, from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven. That's a BLANK CHECK, friend!

cards.question: True or false: Ahaz takes the LORD up on the offer and asks for a sign.

cards.text: Ahaz replies, "I will not ask; I will not test the LORD." The man gets handed a blank check from God and slides it right back across the table.

cards.question: Ahaz refuses to ask for a sign. How does Isaiah answer him?

answers.text: He asks if they will try God's patience
He praises Ahaz for honoring God's name
He agrees and walks away without a word

cards.text: Isaiah says, "Will you try the patience of my God as well?" Ahaz may have turned down a sign, but Isaiah isn't finished.

cards.question: True or false: since Ahaz refused to ask, there will be no sign at all.
The Lord Himself will give the sign: the virgin will give birth to a son and will call Him ___.

cards.text: Immanuel. Matthew quotes this very verse about the birth of Jesus, and he tells us the name means God with us (Matthew 1:22-23).
Isaiah says that by the time the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey. And Isaiah has news about those two kings Ahaz dreads.

cards.question: True or false: before the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, the land of the two kings Ahaz dreads will be laid waste.

cards.text: Good news for Ahaz, right? Hold that thought, friend, because Isaiah warns of a time unlike any since the day Ephraim separated from Judah, when the LORD will bring the king of Assyria.

cards.question: Isaiah warns of a time unlike any since Ephraim separated from Judah. Who will the LORD bring it on?

cards.text: The king of Assyria is coming, and Isaiah describes that day in pictures. First, the LORD will whistle to the flies at the farthest streams of the Nile and to the bees in the land of Assyria.

cards.question: True or false: when the LORD whistles, the flies and bees stay put at the Nile and in Assyria.

cards.text: They come and settle in the ravines, the rocks, the thornbushes and the watering holes, like sprinkles when I rip the bag open too fast. Then Isaiah says the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates.

cards.question: Isaiah names the razor the Lord will hire from beyond the Euphrates. Who is it?

cards.text: That razor shaves the head, the hair of the legs, and removes the beard too. My mustache is my HANDS, friend, so that one hits me right where I live.
Then Isaiah says that on that day, a man will raise a young cow and two sheep.

cards.question: True or false: the man's young cow and two sheep give so little milk that he has nothing to eat.
Isaiah says all who remain in the land will eat the same two things. What are they?

cards.text: Curds and honey, the same words Isaiah used about the boy back in verse 15. Then Isaiah turns to every place that had a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver.

cards.question: On that day, what will be found in the places that once had a thousand valuable vines?

cards.text: A thousand shekels of vineyard, and now the land is covered with briers and thorns. Looks like the back of my old junk drawer, only POINTIER.

cards.question: True or false: with the land covered in briers and thorns, men will go there with bow and arrow.

cards.text: And the hills once tilled by the hoe? For fear of the briers and thorns, Isaiah says, you will no longer walk them.

cards.question: Nobody will walk the hills once tilled by the hoe, so they'll become places for oxen to graze and ___ to trample.
